feature: Every panel row has its name in one column
summary: Appearance, Effects, Text and Layout now draw their rows like the video sections and the mock: a small grey name in one left column with its control beside it. A video document's panel reads as one panel, not two.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The walk is Scripts/playtest/panel-rows-read-as-one-column-walk.json.

try.do: Open a screen recording, press T, click the canvas, type a title and press Command Return.
Scroll the panel to Text and Appearance: Font, Size, Weight, Opacity and Blending each sit on one line, the names in the same column as Playhead and Fade above.
Scroll on to the title's Shadow: Style, Color, Kind and every slider sit beside their names.
Click the recording's clip on the timeline and look at Sound, Fades, Appearance and Captions together.
Drag the panel's left edge in as far as it goes: a row whose control will not fit drops it under the name, and the panel stays inside its dock.
Open a plain picture, draw a rectangle and add a Shadow: the picture panel reads the same way.
Compare with the mock's Properties panel (left) and the app now (right).

evaluate: Does the panel now read as one thing when you scroll from Time down to Captions?
Is the grey name small enough to stay out of the way but still easy to read while redlining?
At the narrowest dock, is Opacity dropping its track under its name better than a cramped track beside it?
Are the Effects settings, stepped in under their effect with their own column, clear enough, or should they line up with Appearance's controls?
Is Size and Weight as two rows, rather than side by side, worth the extra height?
rough: Side by side with video.html PROPERTIES: names, size, colour and the 76pt column match. The mock's property rows show a number box alone; Appearance and Effects keep a track beside the box, the way the mock's Audio Level and Duck rows draw a bar beside the name.

The Effects settings take their column from their own stepped-in start, so their controls sit 24pt right of Appearance's. The mock's frame has Effects folded shut, so there is nothing to measure that against.
Menu values in the Layout section of a screen (Left, Top) are still the callout size, bigger than the mock's 11.5pt select text. Only the names were in scope here.
The Fill and Outline rows keep their tick in front of the name, so their names start 24pt in; their swatches still land on the shared control line.
Current is unchanged: all of this sits behind a Next switch in the Experiments window (The panel, 'Every panel row has its name in one column'), on by default in Next.
